mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates weakening consumer demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies report lower earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between RSAFS drops and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within two months signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic uncertainty rises.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals strengthening supply-side activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth accelerates.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 1% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a high level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment remains bullish.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of instances despite the signal, or the correlation between high HOUST levels and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a decrease in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals a potential deflationary environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real interest rates rise.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases and CPIAUCSL decreases simultaneously
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the interaction effect between FEDFUNDS increases and CPIAUCSL decreases is not statistically significant in predicting negative SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as economic optimism rises.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases simultaneously
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the interaction effect between PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases is not statistically significant in predicting positive SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a decrease in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% quarter-over-quarter during a period of high consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals stagflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic uncertainty and inflationary pressures rise.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases > 0.5% quarter-over-quarter with high CPIAUCSL
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the interaction effect between GDPC1 decreases and high CPIAUCSL is not statistically significant in predicting negative SPX returns (p > 0.05).
